reference: R limma::lmFit + limma::eBayes(trend = TRUE | FALSE), called whole
note: Each case's design is the one the toolkit builds for its analysis_type from the sample labels beside it, and the second coefficient is tested. df_total is limma's pmin(df.residual + df.prior, sum(df.residual)) and every p here is computed on it; df_pooled is sum(df.residual), recorded so a reader can see where the cap binds. s2_prior is the prior variance per feature (constant under the global prior).

cases.name: global_infinite_prior
cases.note: 8 features, 3 vs 3, equal residual variances: df.prior is infinite and df.total is the pooled 8 x 4 = 32, not infinity

cases.name: global_large_finite_prior
cases.note: 5 features, 3 vs 3, residual variances spread just past their sampling variance: df.prior is finite, but df.residual + df.prior exceeds the pooled 20

cases.name: global_cap_does_not_bind
cases.note: 40 features, 6 vs 7, heterogeneous noise: df.residual + df.prior is far below the pooled 440, so the cap changes nothing

cases.name: trend_infinite_prior
cases.note: limma-trend over 12 features spanning 8..19 log2 with equal residual variances: the trend is flat, df.prior is infinite and df.total is the pooled 12 x 4 = 48

cases.name: trend_unpaired
cases.note: 300 features over 12..28 log2, 4 vs 4, variance falling with intensity and scattered about the curve (true prior df 6): spline df 4, finite df.prior, cap does not bind

cases.name: trend_twenty_features
cases.note: 20 features, 3 vs 3: spline df 3 (one interior knot at the median of Amean)

cases.name: trend_five_features
cases.note: 5 features, 3 vs 3: spline df 2, so the trend is a straight line in Amean (no interior knot); a large df.prior and only 20 pooled df, so the cap binds

cases.name: trend_paired
cases.note: 120 features, 6 subjects Pre then Post, design [1, Post, subject dummies]: the subject block removes a 1.5 log2 spread; spline df 4, finite df.prior

cases.name: trend_linear
cases.note: 80 features at weeks 0, 2, 4, 6, 12 (three samples each), design [1, week], the slope tested: spline df 4, finite df.prior

cases.name: trend_missing_values_legacy
cases.note: 150 features, 4 vs 4, some with one NaN per arm (residual df 5 or 4 instead of 6), eBayes(trend = TRUE, legacy = TRUE): fitFDist's moments over unequal df, which is the toolkit's estimator; limma's default for unequal df (fitFDistUnequalDF1) is not

cases.name: global_missing_arm_legacy
cases.note: 8 complete features plus 8 observed only in arm B, 3 vs 3: the B-only rows have no contrast (NA) but 2 residual df each, which go into the prior and the pool (48, not 32); df.prior is infinite, so the cap binds

cases.name: trend_missing_arm_legacy
cases.note: 150 features, 4 vs 4; every 10th has arm A entirely missing (no contrast, 3 residual df, still in the trend and the pool), every 13th one NaN in arm B

cases.name: trend_paired_missing_subject_legacy

cases.name: global_zero_variance
cases.note: 40 features plus 3 whose replicates agree exactly within each arm (residual variance 0), 4 vs 4: fitFDist floors every variance at 1e-5 x the median and fits the prior with them, rather than dropping them
